chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a bondwoman who was mudabbarah, who had absconded from her master for years, then came after her master had died with children and much property; and two witnesses testified for her that her master had made her mudabbarah during his lifetime before she absconded.
He said: "I hold that all that is with her belongs to the heirs."
I said: "And is she not freed from one-third of her master's estate?"
He said: "No. She absconded in disobedience to Allah and to her master, so absconding invalidated the tadbīr."

key_terms.أَبَقَتْ: She absconded or fled from her master.
key_terms.التَّدْبِيرَ: The declaration that a slave is to be freed upon the master's death.
key_terms.الْإِبَاقُ: Absconding of a slave, treated here as a legally consequential act.
key_terms.الْوَرَثَةِ: The heirs entitled to the estate after the master's death.
key_terms.ثُلُثِ: One-third of the estate, the portion relevant to tadbīr execution.
key_terms.سَيِّدِهَا: Her master, whose ownership and declaration are legally relevant.
key_terms.مُدَبَّرَةٍ: A bondwoman granted conditional freedom upon the death of her master.

ai.seo_question: Does a slave woman's absconding invalidate tadbir and affect inheritance rights?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a mudabbarah bondwoman who absconded from her master and later returned after his death. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام rules that her absconding nullified the tadbīr, so she is not freed from one-third of the estate and what she had with her belongs to the heirs.
